findings.title: Pin and verify the remote installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: This build downloads and executes whatever content the mutable URL (or any redirect target) serves at build time. A compromised or changed endpoint therefore executes arbitrary code in the image build and changes produced images without a source-controlled reviewable artifact.

findings.title: Propagate installer download failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Docker RUN uses /bin/sh -c, whose pipeline status is the final `sh` command. If curl fails before writing a script (for example, DNS or TLS failure), `sh` receives empty input and exits successfully, so the image can build without the intended installed dependency.

findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer
findings.whyItBreaks: Every build fetches and executes whatever https://example.com/install.sh serves at that moment. A compromised, changed, or intercepted upstream response can execute arbitrary code in the image build and produce a malicious artifact; curl's silent mode also obscures download errors.

findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer
findings.whyItBreaks: Every image build fetches and executes whatever content is currently served by example.com/install.sh. A compromised, replaced, or intercepted upstream script executes during the build and can alter the resulting image or exfiltrate build-time secrets.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key failure in the public helper
findings.whyItBreaks: LoadOrDefault discards ErrMissing and returns "", making a missing key indistinguishable from a present key whose stored value is legitimately empty. As an exported API, every caller is forced to treat lookup failure as real data.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key error
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but this exported API discards that signal and returns "", making absence indistinguishable from a present key whose value is empty. Callers cannot safely decide whether to use, persist, or report the returned value.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors
findings.whyItBreaks: LoadOrDefault discards ErrMissing and returns "", which is also a valid stored map value. Any caller cannot distinguish an absent key from a present key with an empty value; as a public API, this forces every future caller to conflate those cases.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously Run did not return until every job result had been sent. The new goroutines allow it to return immediately, so a caller that closes or repurposes results after Run returns can race with sends and panic with "send on closed channel". It also makes result delivery order nondeterministic.

findings.title: Wait for spawned result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, Run returned only after every job result had been sent. It now returns immediately after launching goroutines, so a caller that treats return as completion can close results and cause a later goroutine to panic with "send on closed channel"; it can also observe incomplete results at return.

findings.title: Wait for result goroutines before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, Run returned only after every result had been written. The new goroutines outlive Run, so a caller that closes or reuses the results channel once Run returns can race with pending sends and panic; callers also cannot rely on all jobs being complete at return.

findings.title: Use an available github.com/example/lib release
findings.whyItBreaks: github.com/example/lib@v1.2.1 returns HTTP 404 from proxy.golang.org. Any build or dependency-download path that resolves this direct requirement cannot obtain the module.

score.error: critic produced no summary or checked list (likely malformed output)

findings.title: Require admin status before allowing record deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: A session with isAdmin=false and a matching tenantId now receives true, granting delete permission to every user in that tenant. Previously, deletion required both tenant membership and admin status.

findings.title: Require admin status and tenant match before deleting
findings.whyItBreaks: Using `||` authorizes any non-admin session to delete records in its tenant and authorizes admins to delete records in other tenants. The prior policy required both conditions, so this is a deletion authorization bypass.

findings.title: Require administrator status before deleting records
findings.whyItBreaks: With isAdmin=false and matching tenant IDs, this now returns true, allowing any tenant member to delete a record. The prior policy required both tenant scope and administrator status.

findings.title: Preserve invalid-settings errors
findings.whyItBreaks: Malformed JSON or invalid settings formerly threw to the caller; they now become a valid-looking default Settings value. updateFontSize then changes its font size and calls save, replacing the original persisted value with {"theme":"light","fontSize":<size>} rather than reporting the corruption.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-settings errors
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid JSON or an invalid settings field previously threw from parseSettings; this catch now returns legitimate defaults instead. updateFontSize consequently treats corrupted input as valid and saves {"theme":"light","fontSize":size}, overwriting the stored settings rather than surfacing the corruption.

findings.title: Propagate invalid settings instead of replacing them with defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: Malformed or schema-invalid stored settings previously threw and prevented updateFontSize from calling save. They now become {theme:"light",fontSize:14}; updateFontSize then changes the font size and persists that fallback, silently discarding the prior theme/value rather than exposing the corrupted input.

findings.whyItBreaks: For a non-exact multiple, floor rounds away the final page: pageCount(21, 10) returns 2 even though 3 pages are needed to represent all items. As an exported helper, this exposes an incorrect result to callers.

findings.title: Keep artifacts aligned with the reported branch commit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any branch other than "verified", builtFrom remains build.ref(branch) while artifacts are fetched from build.ref("verified"). Consumers receive a report claiming one commit was built but listing artifacts from another commit.

findings.title: Use the requested branch when selecting artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: For any branch whose ref differs from "verified", the report declares builtFrom as that branch's commit but returns artifacts from the verified commit. Consumers therefore receive a self-contradictory report and can publish or inspect artifacts for the wrong build.

findings.title: Keep report artifacts aligned with builtFrom
findings.whyItBreaks: buildFrom remains the requested branch's commit, but artifacts are fetched from the unrelated "verified" ref. When those refs differ, the report falsely attributes verified artifacts to the branch commit.

findings.title: Restore the requested entry limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For every positive limit, recentEntries now returns all entries rather than at most limit. renderFeed passes 20 at line 9; when all has more than 20 entries, its copy loop extends the initially 20-slot output array and returns more than 20 entries.

findings.title: Restore the limit before returning entries
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit smaller than all.length, this returns every reversed entry instead of at most limit. renderFeed passes 20, so inputs with more than 20 entries produce an output larger than its intended 20-entry page.

findings.title: Restore the requested entry limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For every positive limit, this returns the entire reversed input instead of at most `limit` entries. renderFeed passes 20 at src/feed.ts:9, then copies every returned entry, so feeds longer than 20 produce output longer than 20.

findings.title: Keep entry-count aligned with rendered rows
findings.whyItBreaks: For input containing stale entries, the data rows contain only live entries while `# entry-count` still reports all input entries. Consumers that use the header to validate or preallocate for the rows receive contradictory manifest data.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, it is omitted from rows but `# entry-count` still uses `entries.length`. Consumers that use the header to validate or preallocate for manifest rows receive an incorrect count.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest rows
findings.whyItBreaks: When any entry is stale, the output omits its row but still emits `# entry-count` using `entries.length`. Consumers relying on that header will expect more rows than the manifest contains.

findings.title: Restore the removed legacy ID formatter
findings.whyItBreaks: FormatLegacyID is an exported package API that previously produced LEG-prefixed identifiers. Removing it makes any existing consumer calling ids.FormatLegacyID fail to compile on upgrade; no replacement or deprecation path is provided.

findings.title: Restore FormatLegacyID compatibility
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the exported FormatLegacyID function makes any existing consumer of example.com/app/ids that calls it fail to compile on upgrade. The repository has no major-version module boundary or migration path for this API removal.

findings.title: Preserve the shippingQuote export
findings.whyItBreaks: shippingQuote was an exported function from this module before this change, but it is no longer exported. Existing consumers importing it from src/orders will fail to compile or load after upgrade.

findings.title: Return a string from execute
findings.whyItBreaks: execute is exported with a string return contract, but every invocation now throws "always fails". This makes the public API unusable for all inputs and regresses its prior uppercase transformation.

findings.title: Restore execute’s string result
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported execute function unconditionally throws, so every caller loses the prior uppercase-string behavior and cannot receive the declared string result.

findings.title: Restore execution instead of always throwing
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call to the public execute(input) API now throws "always fails" and returns no string, replacing the prior uppercase transformation.

findings.title: Keep viewers eligible for the read-only handler path
findings.whyItBreaks: For an active viewer below the attempt limit, the new role guard returns false, so handle() returns "rejected" at line 24. The subsequent viewer branch at line 25, which returns "read-only", is now unreachable; before this change the same request reached that branch.

findings.title: Preserve the active viewer read-only path
findings.whyItBreaks: An active viewer below the attempt limit previously passed isEligible and handle returned "read-only". The new predicate rejects that same request before handle reaches its viewer branch, making the existing read-only behavior unreachable.

findings.title: Preserve viewer access to the read-only path
findings.whyItBreaks: An active viewer below the attempt limit now fails isEligible and handle returns "rejected" at line 24. Before this change, that same request reached line 25 and returned "read-only"; the explicit viewer branch is now dead.

findings.title: Allow unpaid orders to save as drafts
findings.whyItBreaks: For { state: "draft", payment: "missing" }, canProceed now returns false, so saveDraft returns "blocked" at src/actions.ts:9. Saving a draft is distinct from submitting it and was previously allowed regardless of payment.

findings.title: Keep unpaid drafts saveable
findings.whyItBreaks: For an order with state "draft" and payment "missing", this predicate now returns false. saveDraft uses the same predicate and returns "blocked", whereas this order was previously saveable. Requiring payment to submit is valid, but it should not prevent persisting an unpaid draft.

findings.title: Keep unpaid drafts saveable
findings.whyItBreaks: Adding `order.payment === "paid"` to the shared predicate makes `saveDraft` return "blocked" for `{ state: "draft", payment: "missing" }`. Payment may govern submission, but it should not prevent persisting an unpaid draft.

findings.title: Build files from the advertised commit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any channel whose head differs from "stable", the returned Snapshot.commit identifies the channel head, but Snapshot.files contains the stable commit's files. Consumers receive a self-inconsistent snapshot and can publish or inspect the wrong revision.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the requested channel commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned Snapshot reports commit=headCommit(channel), but its files are loaded from headCommit("stable"). When the requested channel differs from stable, consumers receive a self-contradictory snapshot: its commit and files describe different revisions.

findings.title: Read files from the selected channel commit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any requested channel whose head differs from stable, Snapshot.commit is the channel head from line 13 but Snapshot.files is read from stable. Consumers receive an internally inconsistent snapshot and may publish or inspect files that do not belong to the reported commit.

findings.title: Honor the limit argument
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=3)` still returns 10 entries because the body hard-codes `max_count = 10`; the new parameter's observable limit contract is not implemented.

findings.title: Honor the requested result limit
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=3)` still returns 10 entries because the implementation unconditionally assigns `max_count = 10`. The new public parameter promises caller-controlled output sizing but has no effect.

findings.title: Honor the requested result limit
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=3)` still returns ten items because the body always assigns `max_count = 10`. The new public parameter promises an observable cap but has no effect.

findings.title: Validate positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but int(value) accepts 0 and negative values. Callers can therefore receive a negative charge or a zero charge through an API that claims to enforce positivity.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public name promises a positive integer, but int(value) accepts 0 and negative values. Consequently charge('-1') returns -100 and charge('0') returns 0 instead of rejecting values outside the promised contract.

findings.title: Reject non-positive values in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public helper now promises a positive integer, but int(value) accepts 0 and negative values. Consequently charge("-1") returns -100 cents, violating the advertised contract for callers that rely on this validator.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously the function updated a copy and left df unchanged. It now writes through to df, so callers that retain and reuse the original DataFrame observe its values unexpectedly changed after calling apply_values.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, apply_values returned a modified copy while leaving df unchanged. The new assignment writes directly into df, so callers that reuse the input after calling this function will observe their original data unexpectedly changed.

findings.title: Preserve the caller DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation copied df before applying the mapping. The changed code writes through to df and returns that same object, so callers that retain or reuse their input observe unintended value changes.

findings.title: Enforce the positive-integer contract
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-1")` returns -1 and `parse_positive_int("0")` returns 0, contrary to the public function's stated positive-value contract. External callers can rely on the renamed API and receive non-positive results.

findings.title: Reject non-positive input in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-1")` returns `-1`, despite its public name promising a positive result. Its caller then computes `charge("-1")` as `-100`, so negative amounts are accepted rather than rejected or normalized.

findings.title: Enforce the positive-value contract
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-5")` returns `-5` and `parse_positive_int("0")` returns `0`, contradicting the newly public positive-value contract. Its current caller therefore produces a negative charge (`charge("-5") == -500`) without rejecting the amount.

findings.title: Remove the debug call that consumes `items`
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` evaluates and returns the owned `Vec<String>`; as a statement, that returned vector is dropped. The subsequent `items.len()` therefore borrows a moved value and fails compilation.

findings.title: Avoid moving items before computing its length
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` evaluates and returns the owned `Vec<String>`, which is then discarded by the semicolon. This moves `items`, so `items.len()` on line 3 fails with Rust error E0382 (borrow of moved value).

findings.title: Avoid moving `items` before reading its length
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` evaluates and returns `items` by value, moving the Vec. Line 3 then borrows the moved value with `items.len()`, preventing the crate from compiling.

findings.title: Compute paths from the returned revision
findings.whyItBreaks: When `pinnedTag` resolves to a revision older than `latest`, `changedPaths` excludes changes between that pinned revision and `latest`, but `fromRevision` still tells consumers to replay those paths on the pinned revision. Consumers therefore receive an incomplete changeset.

findings.title: Compute paths from the replay baseline
findings.whyItBreaks: `fromRevision` remains the revision resolved from `pinnedTag`, but `changedPaths` is now read relative to the unrelated `latest` revision. A consumer replaying these paths on `fromRevision`, as the public `Changeset` contract requires, can receive paths for the wrong base revision.

findings.title: Compute paths against the returned base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: Changeset.fromRevision remains the revision resolved from pinnedTag, but changedPaths is now computed from latest. Consumers replay these paths on fromRevision (as documented), so when pinnedTag is not latest they receive a path set computed against a different base and can apply or report the wrong changes.

findings.title: Update query to use renamed email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration renames users.email to users.contact_email, src/query.sql still executes SELECT email FROM users, which fails because email no longer exists.

findings.title: Update queries to use the renamed email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, `users.email` no longer exists, but `src/query.sql:1` still executes `SELECT email FROM users`. Any deployment that applies the migration then uses that query will fail with a missing-column SQL error.

findings.title: Update queries for the renamed email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, users.email no longer exists, but src/query.sql:1 still executes SELECT email FROM users. Any consumer running that query after upgrading will receive a missing-column database error.

findings.title: Restore runtime-supplied billing credentials
findings.whyItBreaks: A production-looking billing API key is now committed to source and returned in every environment. This exposes the credential to repository readers and makes development, CI, and deployed instances all authenticate as the same live billing account instead of using their configured secret.

findings.title: Restore environment-sourced billing credentials
findings.whyItBreaks: This commits a `bk_live_` credential to source control and ignores each deployment's BILLING_API_KEY. Anyone with repository access can use the billing credential, and rotating or revoking it will break every deployment rather than allowing per-environment replacement.

findings.title: Restore environment-based billing credential loading
findings.whyItBreaks: Every deployment now uses the credential committed to source control, exposing it to all repository readers and preventing separate credentials or rotation through BILLING_API_KEY. The previous unset-key failure is also removed, so a missing deployment secret is silently masked by this shared credential.

findings.whyItBreaks: For an administrator with an archived project, this new early return produces "forbidden" and skips db.delete. The base behavior purged exactly that combination.

findings.title: Restore default settings when configuration is missing
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when path does not exist (app/config.py:6-7). startup now immediately subscripts that None value, raising TypeError instead of returning the prior default worker count of 1.

findings.title: Restore handling for missing settings files
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when the path does not exist (app/config.py:6-7). The removed fallback allowed startup to use one worker; startup now evaluates None["workers"] and raises TypeError, breaking the prior no-config startup path.

findings.title: Restore the missing-settings fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when path does not exist (line 7). Without the removed fallback, startup evaluates settings["workers"] on None and raises TypeError, breaking startup for a previously supported absent-config path.

findings.title: Propagate failed gateway charges
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge now logs it and returns nil. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a declined/failed charge from a completed one and can treat unpaid orders as paid. Before this change, the error reached Charge's caller via the wrapped return at pay/charge.go:17.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge logs it and then returns nil. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a rejected/failed charge from a completed charge and may treat an unpaid transaction as successful.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit fails, Charge logs the error then returns nil. Callers cannot distinguish a declined/failed charge from a completed one and may mark payment as successful.

findings.title: Restore tenant identity in the cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: `settingsFor` still fetches values scoped by `tenantId` (line 15), but the cache now keys only on `name`. After tenant A reads `name`, tenant B reading that same name returns tenant A's cached value without calling its store, exposing cross-tenant settings and returning incorrect configuration.

findings.title: Preserve the exported invalidate call contract
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing the exported function from `invalidate(tenantId, name)` to `invalidate(name)` is a source-breaking public API change. Existing TypeScript consumers fail to compile; existing JavaScript consumers pass the tenant ID as the sole effective argument and invalidate the wrong cache entry.

findings.title: Include tenant ID in the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A reads setting `theme`, `cache` stores it as `settings:theme`. A later `settingsFor(tenantB, "theme", store)` hits that same key at line 13 and returns tenant A's value without calling `store.fetch`, breaking tenant isolation and serving incorrect settings.

findings.title: Preserve the exported invalidate call signature
findings.whyItBreaks: `invalidate` is exported, and changing it from `(tenantId, name)` to `(name)` is a source-breaking API change for existing TypeScript consumers, which will fail argument-count checking when upgraded.

findings.title: Include the tenant ID in the cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A caches setting `name`, a request for the same `name` from tenant B hits `settings:${name}` and returns tenant A's value without calling `store.fetch(tenantB, name)`. The previous key included `tenantId`.

findings.title: Serialize same-SKU reservations across persistence
findings.whyItBreaks: The stock update occurs after an await. Two callers reserving a SKU with count 1 both read 1, both await save(sku, 0), then both return true. This confirms two reservations for one unit and loses the second decrement.

findings.title: Serialize reservations for each SKU
findings.whyItBreaks: Two concurrent reserve("sku") calls can both read the same positive remaining value before either await completes. Both save the same decremented count and return true, so one unit can be reserved twice.

findings.title: Serialize concurrent reservations before awaiting persistence
findings.whyItBreaks: Two concurrent reserve calls can both read the same positive count, both await save(sku, 0), then both return true. Previously reserve was synchronous, so the second call observed the decremented in-memory stock and returned false.

findings.title: Keep retry delay units consistent
findings.whyItBreaks: `backoff(0)` now returns 1,000 milliseconds for `schedulePoll`, but `retry` still calls `sleep(backoff(a) * 1000)`. A first failed retry therefore waits 1,000,000 ms (16.7 minutes) instead of the previous 1,000 ms; later retries can wait up to 30 minutes.

findings.title: Keep retry delays in milliseconds after changing backoff units
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff(0) now returns 2,000 milliseconds, but retry() still multiplies it by 1,000 before passing it to sleep(). A retry after its first failure waits 2,000,000 ms (about 33 minutes) instead of 2,000 ms; later retries similarly become 1,000× slower.

findings.title: Update retry to consume millisecond backoff values
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff(0) now returns 1,000 ms, but retry still calls sleep(backoff(a) * 1000). A retry after its first failure therefore waits 1,000,000 ms (~16.7 minutes) instead of 1 second; capped retries wait 30,000,000 ms (~8.3 hours) instead of 30 seconds.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error
findings.whyItBreaks: The new deferred Close call discards its error. Previously Save returned f.Close()'s error after a successful Flush; callers can now receive nil even when final file close fails, making a failed save indistinguishable from success.

findings.title: Propagate the file-close error
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred Close return value is discarded. Previously a successful Flush still returned f.Close()'s error; now Save returns nil when Close fails, falsely reporting that persistence completed.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred f.Close() discards its error. Previously, successful Flush paths returned f.Close()'s error, so callers could detect a write that failed while finalizing the file; now Save returns nil after a successful flush even if Close fails.

findings.title: Include the page end index when collecting rows
findings.whyItBreaks: The half-open bounds are [start, end), but range(start, end - 1) excludes end - 1. Thus each full page loses its last row and a one-row final page becomes empty; for example, three rows at page_size=2 renders only the first row.

findings.title: Include the final row in each page
findings.whyItBreaks: _window_bounds returns a half-open end bound, but range(start, end - 1) excludes end - 1. Every page loses its last row; with page_size=1, summarize renders every page empty.
